title: CPA Security of ISW-Then-Dummy-Shuffling
summary: The variant can expose pre-shuffled zero encodings as ciphertext data when no data dependencies leak, but its CPA security remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine the $\mathrm{CPA}$ security of the ISW-then-dummy-shuffling Haystack-cipher variant, in which refreshing is performed after ISW. Dummy shuffling refreshes each AND gate by XORing fresh randomness into a dummy slot and $0$ into the main slot, creating a pre-shuffled encoding of zero. For AND gates inside the ISW multiplication gadget, these refreshing bits are not protected by ISW, so the resulting pre-shuffled encodings of zero are included in the ciphertext as intermediate gadget data. The analysis must assume that including this data leaks no data dependencies.

scope.domain: CPA security analysis of an ISW-then-dummy-shuffling Haystack cipher containing intermediate multiplication-gadget data.
assumptions: Including the intermediate gadget data leaks no data dependencies.
parameters: Refreshing order: refreshing is performed after ISW
Dummy-shuffling refresh values: fresh randomness enters a dummy slot and zero enters the main slot
Ciphertext exposure: pre-shuffled zero encodings from AND gates inside the ISW multiplication gadget are included as intermediate data
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the variant's CPA security under the no-data-dependency-leakage assumption.

citations.label: Haystack ciphers : White-box countermeasures as Symmetric encryption

progress.summary: The source explains how to model the ISW-then-dummy-shuffling variation by including exposed intermediate zero encodings in the Haystack ciphertext. It calls for analyzing the variation but provides no CPA-security resolution.
